text:
jon: Heads up — after the kernel swap (commit abc1234) I see a clear 95p tail regression on the continuous batching path. p50 steady ~22ms, p95 jumped from ~88ms -> ~160ms for generation requests. Token throughput looks similar.

maya: Which kernel change exactly? any flamegraphs or perf counters you can paste?

jon: Pasted perf counters from the canary host (short):
```
timestamp: 2026-03-18T09:12:02Z
commit: abc1234 (softmax: aten->atan-softmax micro-optim)
metrics: token_latency_p50=22.4ms token_latency_p95=159.8ms
llc_misses/s: 2.1k -> 9.8k
cycles: 3.2e9 -> 3.5e9
kv_evictions/s: 120 -> 640
batch_size_p95: 1 -> 6 (more large micro-batches observed)
flamegraph: s3://redwood-perf/canaries/2026-03-18/abc1234/flame.svg
```

lee: Those kv_evictions numbers are the smoking gun to me. If the kernel change subtly shifts memory access pattern it can push more pages out of the KV cache, causing extra memcpy/rehydrate work and larger formation delays (we saw batch_size jump). Evictions/s x5 is enough to explain the tail.

ci-bot: deploy: canary abc1234 -> rollouts/edge-2026-03-18 started by @jon. 6 hosts targeted.

maya: Ok — propose a controlled experiment before reverting. Two knobs to probe: micro-batch interval and coalesce jitter. My hypothesis: tighter micro-batch interval with slightly increased jitter will reduce the formation of those unexpectedly large batches and lower eviction pressure. Also reduce token_budget_per_microbatch to limit kernel work per batch.

maya: Proposed canary config (quick):
```json
{
  "experiment": "kb-coalesce-probe-2026-03-18",
  "microbatch_interval_ms": 1.2,
  "coalesce_delay_ms": 3,
  "coalesce_jitter": {"type": "gaussian", "sigma_ms": 0.6},
  "token_budget_per_microbatch": 32,
  "queue_policy": "latency_priority_small_tokens"
}
```

jon: Ran the perf harness (A->B, 2k requests) against the canary hosts with that config: p95 improved to ~92ms (from 160ms) and p50 unchanged. Throughput dropped ~6% on that slot (we lose some batching win). kv_evictions/s down to ~180.

lee: That's promising. Tradeoff looks acceptable if we can recover throughput elsewhere. Suggest adding a secondary policy: keep aggressive batching for long-running large-token requests (e.g., >256 tokens) but prioritize sub-64 token requests for low-latency path — prevents them getting stuck behind huge coalesced batches. Sample routing snippet: 
```
route: {
  "priority_rules": [
    {"if_max_tokens_le": 64, "route": "low_latency_pool"},
    {"else": "standard_coalesce_pool"}
  ]
}
```

maya: Will add that rule to the canary (A/B split 50/50). Also plan to capture kernel symbol traces to see which kernels are selected at the hot paths now (to confirm it's the atan-softmax path causing extra memory churn).

ops-sre: Add guardrails: auto-rollback if token_latency_p95 > 150ms for more than 3 minutes, and alert @eng-runtime if error rate or memory pressure spikes. I'll watch the SLOs for the next 2h.

jon: I'll run a 30m continuous load with kv_inspect on and dump eviction + page-fault traces to s3. Tagging results as s3://redwood-perf/experiments/kb-coalesce-2026-03-18/jon-run1.tar.gz

maya: Nice. Owners: jon (canary + traces), lee (routing tweak + perf analysis), maya (experiment config + A/B orchestration). If the A/B shows consistent p95 < 110ms with <4% throughput loss, we can keep the kernel swap and keep the coalesce tweak. If not, rollback and investigate kernel micro-optim further. :mag: :gear:

ops-sre: noted. I'll post a watch window in #incidents if rollback triggers.
